title: Bias: the dial with no input

introduces.gloss: the number that flows in from the left tube
a dial that scales its input
a dial fed by an always-full tube; it shifts every output

sentences: {machine}Here is a neuron again, drawn in section.
{input}An input flows in from the left, {weight}through its weight dial, {gauge}and the gauge reads the output.
{empty}Now empty the input.
{zero}Zero, times any weight, is still zero.
{stuck}Turn the weight dial all you like. The needle will not move.
{source}So a neuron has a second dial, {full}fed from a tube that is always full.
{bias}This dial is called the bias.|
{shift}It adds the same amount to the output, {always}whatever the input is.
{recap}The weight scales the input. {recap2}The bias shifts the result.
{mark}Together, they can put the needle on any mark.
Your turn. The input is empty. Turn the weight dial two clicks to the right.
The needle stayed at zero. With no input, the weight has nothing to scale.
Now turn the bias dial, until the needle sits on the brass mark.
The bias dial adds its setting straight to the output. Turn it to the right.
On the mark, with no input at all. That is what a bias is for.
Now a puzzle. The input is two, and the mark is at three.
Reach it in six clicks or fewer. The punched holes count your clicks.
On the mark. The weight and the bias shared the work.
Out of clicks. The dials go back to zero.
Each click is half a unit. The weight counts twice here, because the input is two.
Last one. The input is one, and the mark is at minus two. Four clicks.
Below zero, on the mark. Weight and bias can both pull the output down.
Out of clicks. The dials go back to zero.
With an input of one, a click on either dial moves the needle half a unit. Turn them to the left.
